title: AudienceExtensions cannot express an unrecognised presence requirement; it silently becomes None
description:
persona-core/src/audience.rs:61: `require_presence = PresenceLevel::from_str(val).unwrap_or(PresenceLevel::None)`.

The parse error is discarded and the field collapses to the weakest possible value. The `AudienceExtensions` type has no way to represent "a presence requirement was stated but not understood", so no caller can implement fail-closed handling even if it wants to. The one consumer, persona-grpc/src/service.rs:146, compares `ext.require_presence > claim.presence` — with `None` on the left that check always passes, so an audience string of `?persona_require_presence=biometric` (a level this crate does not know yet) is served as if no presence had been requested at all. audience.rs:121-126 tests and locks in exactly this behaviour.

`PresenceLevel` is `#[non_exhaustive]` (assurance.rs:65) precisely because more levels are expected, which guarantees a version skew where a newer relying party asks for a level an older daemon silently ignores.

Note the inconsistency within the same function: the sibling parameter `persona_max_age` does the opposite and returns `AudienceParseError::InvalidMaxAge` on a bad value (audience.rs:65). One malformed persona parameter is a hard error, the other is a silent downgrade.

Fix: return `AudienceParseError::UnknownPresenceLevel(String)` (the enum is already non_exhaustive so adding the variant is free), or keep the raw string in the struct so the caller decides. Either way the API should make fail-closed expressible.
close_reason: Duplicate of persona-5s4b.71 (same defect, filed by a second review agent from a different angle). Merged during review triage; reopen if the angle in this issue is not covered there.
